concerns.text: T027-PROACTIVE mandates 'deterministically random subsample' of the dataset if runtime estimates exceed limits. This violates FR-002 (construct full covariance for harmonized dataset) and Constitution Principle VI (any analysis omitting covariance structure is invalid). The task relaxes the requirement to use the full dataset without explicit spec authorization for subsampling as a fallback.

T015-A/B implement a fallback to 'banded/block-diagonal' approximation if full covariance fails. FR-002 and Constitution Principle VI mandate a 'full covariance matrix'. The tasks provide no mechanism to verify if the 'full' attempt failed or if the fallback is scientifically valid, effectively weakening the requirement to 'full' without a spec-defined exception.

T031 requires reading an 'inflation factor' from config with a default of 2.0. FR-005 and SC-003 define the inflation test with '[deferred]' magnitude. Hardcoding a default value (2.0) in the task without a spec-defined threshold creates an untestable deliverable that does not satisfy the spec's requirement to defer the value.

T033 raises a 'RuntimeError' if CV > 15%. SC-003 defines robustness as 'shifts < 15%' (a success condition to be measured/logged). The task introduces a hard blocking failure that contradicts the spec's intent to 'assess stability' and 'log' results, potentially preventing the generation of final artifacts even if the science is valid but noisy.

T013-A/B fetch arXiv data but omit the 'Reference-Validator Agent' call required by Plan.md (Constitution Principle II) and Constitution Principle II itself. The plan explicitly states the download script 'explicitly calls' the validator, but the task description lacks this implementation step, violating the 'Verified Accuracy' gate.

T038 computes Bayes-factor comparison against the null-simulation baseline (FR-009) but omits the comparison against the 'Kass–Raftery scale (K > 3)' required by SC-002. The task delivers only half of the success criterion, weakening the verification step.
